basics.name: Aidan McLean
basics.label: Full-Stack Developer
basics.status: Research Assistant @ McMaster Faculty of Engineering
basics.lede: I'm a full-stack developer. I build the schema, the API, the interface on top of it, and the server it runs on. Right now that means a research platform at McMaster where researchers benchmark AI battery models, and a storefront and admin console for an independent record label.
basics.contactNote: Open to hearing about backend, full-stack, and infrastructure work. The fastest way to reach me is email.

highlights: Architected and developed a full-stack research platform (Node.js/Express, TypeScript, React, PostgreSQL) that lets researchers submit and benchmark AI battery State-of-Charge models against one another, ranking submissions across 18+ evaluation metrics.

Delivered features end to end across the stack, from REST API endpoints to the React components consuming them, including model submission workflows, results export, an in-app notification system, and an administrative management console.

Designed the PostgreSQL schema (Drizzle ORM) covering authentication, model metadata, and evaluation history, and implemented cookie-based session authentication, rate limiting, and role-based access control across all protected routes.

Built an asynchronous evaluation pipeline that runs each submission in an isolated Docker container, enabling concurrent scoring of multiple models without cross-submission interference, and delivers results through the notification system and email.

Manage deployment on an Ubuntu server (Compute Canada's OpenStack cloud), including NGINX configuration, PM2 process management, and SSL/TLS certificate renewal; incorporate agentic AI development tools (e.g. Claude Code) into the workflow for debugging, code review, and infrastructure scripting.
Customized Drupal Webforms with JavaScript to implement dynamic form behaviour, validation, and improved user experience.
Built front-end integrations with Microsoft APIM to apply business logic, route requests securely, and connect forms to backend services.
Developed a TypeScript front-end application that integrated with an internal GIS map server to retrieve and visualize location-based data.
Picked up Drupal, APIM, and Power Automate on the job and put them straight to use on live production forms.
Documented APIs, workflows, and form logic so other developers could pick up the work without re-deriving it.

projects.name: Record Label E-Commerce Platform
projects.summary: A production storefront, admin console, and in-person point-of-sale for an independent record label, with dual-currency pricing, idempotent order processing, role-based admin access, and per-currency reporting.
projects.detail: A TypeScript monorepo built with Turborepo and pnpm workspaces: two Next.js 16 / React 19 applications over four shared internal packages, about 35K lines across 36 Postgres tables and 24 versioned migrations. Prices are set per currency instead of being converted, so USD and CAD are separate columns resolved through a three-level chain, and every subsystem that reads a price has to track which currency it came from.
highlights: Found and fixed a silent pricing bug. SQL min() ignores NULLs, so incomplete price rows produced plausible but unbuyable prices. Added a bool_and completeness guard in both the query layer and the admin form.

Built currency switching with no layout shift that keeps Incremental Static Regeneration working. Both prices render server-side, and a pre-paint inline script plus CSS picks one, so product pages stay statically generated while each visitor sees their own currency.

Made Stripe Checkout idempotent end to end, with signature-verified webhooks, a reconciliation cron to catch lost events, and inventory reserved at session creation with automatic sweeping of abandoned checkouts.

Built a channel- and currency-aware analytics layer that never sums across currencies, uses a fixed default so figures do not change between page loads, and labels excluded orders instead of reporting a partial number as a total.

Shipped a mobile-first point-of-sale for live shows, covering cash and e-transfer sales, oversell-tolerant stock decrements through an inventory ledger, per-currency line re-pricing, and cost snapshots recorded in the sale's own currency to keep margin accurate.

Built role-based access control on better-auth with granular permission statements across three roles, checked on every admin route and server action, with an append-only audit log on all money, inventory, and user changes.

Secured the public endpoints with Zod validation before any database access, IP-keyed rate limiting on unauthenticated routes, honeypot bot filtering, parameterized queries, CSP headers, and generic client errors that keep detail server-side.

Set up the release workflow after a schema-lag outage. Migrations deploy before code, GitHub Actions applies them to Neon on merge, and a typecheck, lint, test, and build gate runs across all 16 workspace tasks.

projects.name: SoC Model Benchmarking Platform
projects.summary: A research platform where teams upload AI battery State-of-Charge models and have them scored against a shared benchmark. Submissions are graded on 18+ metrics and ranked against every other entry.
projects.detail: Every submission is arbitrary researcher code, so each one runs in its own Docker container through an asynchronous evaluation pipeline. Multiple models score at the same time without interfering with each other, and results come back through an in-app notification system and email. Auth, model metadata, and evaluation history live in a PostgreSQL schema I designed with Drizzle ORM, behind cookie-based sessions, rate limiting, and role-based access control.
